clue.text: Competent troupe, and fun to meet socially

parts.note: competent means good at something
a troupe of actors is a company

explanation.surface: Praise for a theatrical troupe who are both skilled performers and pleasant to spend an evening with.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone enjoyable to be with at a party or dinner is said to be pleasant to have around in this idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Spirit, German beer and a mixer drink

parts.note: gin is a spirit
ale is a beer

explanation.surface: A list of drinks at a bar: spirits, a German lager, and something to top them up with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' tempts as GINGER (mettle), but it is just GIN; German adds GER.
explanation.definitionFit: This fizzy, spicy soft drink is commonly poured with whisky or brandy as a mixer.

clue.text: Noted drama based on Scripture proves effective

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, so it rests on it

parts.note: an opera is drama set to musical notes
NT, the New Testament, is Scripture

explanation.surface: A musical drama drawn from the Bible turns out to work well.
explanation.definitionFit: Operant is a formal word for producing an effect, that is, active or working.

clue.text: Disheartened about cleric being rebuked

indicators.note: the word for disheartened goes around the cleric, enclosing him

parts.note: cored means having had the heart removed
Rect. is the abbreviation for rector, a cleric

explanation.surface: A clergyman, dispirited, is given a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' is read literally: an apple cored has lost its heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put right sharply, scolded for a fault, is a sense of being told off.

clue.text: A wood from Alabama pleasing to the eye

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the letters of the following words, straddling them

explanation.surface: A forest in the American South that is lovely to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: This tree, whose timber is prized for furniture, is a kind of hardwood.

clue.text: He gets a lift, from a sextet, to a hill

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A man hitches a ride, starting from a group of six and ending at a hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets a lift' suggests hitchhiking; the flier is lifted by his wings into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot rises into the air, so he is one who is borne aloft.

clue.text: Still without a small ingredient for bread-making

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside: the word for still surrounds the other letters

parts.note: still, as in 'still here', means yet

explanation.surface: A recipe note: keep going, leaving out one minor item needed to bake a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The fungus that makes dough rise is a raising agent baked into loaves.

clue.text: Roam over the mountains

definitions.meaning: to roam is to wander freely over an area
a chain of mountains, as in the Pennine chain

explanation.surface: An invitation to wander across the high peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander widely is to rove; and a line of peaks is a mountain chain.

clue.text: Enjoyed food outside pub -like successful author

indicators.note: the word for enjoyed food is placed around the pub, which sits within it

parts.note: relished means ate with enjoyment

explanation.surface: A writer celebrating with a meal outside a pub after a book succeeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular writer's book sells out and is printed again in a new edition.

clue.text: Upbraid agent bringing chap in free

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is an agent

indicators.note: the chap is put inside the word for free

parts.note: to rid is to free, as in rid of
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Telling off an agent who brings a man in for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To upbraid is to scold someone formally, a synonym.

clue.text: Have no fear! It's a powerful battleship

definitions.meaning: ..., read as two words, means fear nothing
the name of a class of big-gun warships begun in 1906

explanation.surface: A rousing slogan for a mighty warship.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Dreadnought gave her name to a type of heavily armed battleship; the two words also mean fear nothing.

clue.text: Before the wise man's forecast

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A prediction made earlier by a wise elder.
explanation.definitionFit: A presage is an omen or sign of what is to come, a prediction.

clue.text: Give the book a name "The Measure of The Baron", perhaps

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of width
Baron is an example of a title of nobility, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: Choosing a title for a novel, perhaps a story about a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks Baron as one example of a rank or style.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a heading to a book is to call it something, to dub it.

clue.text: Explosion results in mild expletive

definitions.meaning: a gentle curse said in annoyance, like 'drat'

explanation.surface: A bang that prompts someone to curse softly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden detonation is a bang; the word is also a mild oath.

clue.text: Allowed to get reforms altered

indicators.note: reforms means forms again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something was permitted, provided rules were changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerated means put up with or permitted, a synonym of allowed.

clue.text: Largely an impairment of the vocal cords

indicators.note: an impairment damages the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medical note describing a damaged voice box.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective refers to the voice box, where the vocal cords sit.

clue.text: When interrogated about stipulation, I gave evidence

indicators.note: the word for interrogated wraps around the other letters

parts.note: to be questioned closely is to be tested
if is a condition or stipulation, as in ifs and buts

explanation.surface: A witness questioned on a condition takes the stand.
explanation.definitionFit: To give evidence in court is to swear to the facts as a witness.

clue.text: I verbally disparage a North European

indicators.note: verbally means spoken, so these words are heard as a sound

parts.note: to slander is to disparage

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to speaking ill of a Scandinavian.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'I slander' runs together into a sound like the answer; 'verbally' puts the disparaging word into speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Iceland, an island nation of northern Europe.

clue.text: Judge the rarebit to be cooked

indicators.note: cooking mixes things up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A judge decides the Welsh rarebit is to be grilled.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast, a British snack.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is one who settles a dispute, a referee or judge.

clue.text: A lariat used by the Spanish thus

parts.note: las is the Spanish for the, before a plural noun
so means thus

explanation.surface: A cowboy's rope used by the Spanish, as it happens.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a rope with a noose, used to catch cattle.

clue.text: Confinement at home after telling tales

indicators.note: the piece for at home comes after the first piece

parts.note: telling tales means telling lies
in means at home

explanation.surface: Being stuck at home after spreading gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated term for the period a mother spends in bed around childbirth, called her confinement.

clue.text: Henry and I have reservation in serving fish

parts.note: Hal is a pet name for Henry
a but is an objection or reservation

explanation.surface: Henry and I have doubts about the fish being served.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flatfish of northern seas, a type of edible fish.

clue.text: Transport facilities used by golfers

definitions.meaning: transport connections such as roads and rail
a seaside golf course is known by this name

explanation.surface: Roads and trains for those heading to play golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Transport connections are routes; and a seaside course is called by this word.

clue.text: Up-ended fine piece of bone

indicators.note: in a down clue, up-ended means the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or fine, with the numeral 1 read as I
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A nice bit of bone turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: The shinbone of the lower leg is one bone of the skeleton.

clue.text: Nobbling a Pole in poor health

parts.note: N is the North Pole
ailing means unwell

explanation.surface: Stopping a sick Polish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' is not a person from Poland but a magnetic pole.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail someone is to catch or secure them, as nobbling does.

clue.text: Take horse to stud in Berkshire

annotationWithheld.why: Take horse to stud in Berkshire: DUN + STABLE builds DUNSTABLE, but the definition 'in Berkshire' is wrong (Dunstable is in Bedfordshire) and no source gives the printed text
annotationWithheld.clue: Take horse to stud in Berkshire

clue.text: King George 1st produced grain

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is King George
first is written 1st, with 1 read as I

explanation.surface: The first King George grew corn.
explanation.definitionFit: Grist is corn brought to the mill to be ground into flour.

clue.text: Its aldermen resolved to be up to date

indicators.note: resolved, read as solved again, means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Councillors decide to modernise.
explanation.definitionFit: Streamlined means modernised and efficient, contemporary.
